question: Why are North rentals down on last year since May?
system: Don't say anything that isn't clearly supported by the data. If you are unable to answer something with the data, say so.
answer:
**The data can't tell us why. It does show where and when the gap appears, and it points to one thing that is not the cause.**

**What the data shows** (2026 weeks matched to the same fiscal weeks last year)

| Period | 2026 | 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 Apr to 27 Apr (4 weeks) | 18,879 | 18,786 | +93 (+0.5%) |
| 4 May to 22 Jun (8 weeks) | 38,149 | 41,808 | −3,659 (−8.8%) |

- The 4 May week itself was level with last year (4,686 vs 4,676). The shortfall starts the week after, and it is uneven. The weeks of 18 May and 1 Jun were down only about 100 to 140, while 8 Jun and 15 Jun were down about 890.
- All three depots are down since 4 May: Hollin Cross −1,430 (−8.4%), Petherby −863 (−7.3%) and Scarrow Bridge −1,366 (−10.5%). The decline is not isolated to one depot.
- No North data is missing, so the gap isn't a loading problem.

**Possible links, none of them proven**

- The North price change took effect on 4 May, which is when the gap opens. A staff note from Petherby on 19 May says regulars were unhappy with the new prices and two said they would shop around. That is anecdotal, from one depot, and the data doesn't show whether any customer actually left.
- Weekly volumes did not fall after the price change. Before it (6 Apr to 27 Apr) they ranged from 4,464 to 5,007. After it, they ranged from 4,494 to 5,038. Much of the year-on-year gap comes from last year's rise. The 2025 North total climbed from around 4,700 in April to 5,200–5,700 in late May and June, and 2026 did not follow that rise. So the data doesn't show the price change pushing rentals below their earlier level.

**What I can't determine from this data**

- Whether the price change caused any of the gap, as there is no customer-level, pricing or competitor data.
- Why 2025 rose so strongly in May and June. Seasonality, a one-off event or a promotion are all possible, but nothing here says which.
- Anything about fleet availability, weather or demand in the North, as none of that is included.

The other staff notes (Carrick Stowe, Tidesend, Lowen Quay) concern South and West depots and have no bearing on North.

To go further, I'd need rental data by customer or category, the actual price changes, and ideally earlier years to see whether the May to June rise in 2025 was normal.
